records.author: tokens
records.title: @tokens: - This week on @Solana. A stablecoin from the payment giants, a Nasdaq list...
records.content: - This week on @Solana. A stablecoin from the payment giants, a Nasdaq listing on day two, a securities standard, a Korean bank and a newsroom. - @openstandard. OUSD went live on Solana, backed by Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa. Businesses mint and redeem it free. - Holders. Tokenized-stock holders on Solana hit a record 1.2 million, 775,000 of them new in September. Holders of tokenized commodities passed 70,000, more than double the count on 1 September. - @powerus_usa. Listed on Nasdaq on Thursday, put its own common stock on Solana on Friday. The company announced it itself. - @metaplex. MPL-3643, a standard for permissioned securities. The issuer's rules, from KYC to lockups, are checked on every transfer. - Shinhan Bank. One of Korea's largest banks ran corporate cross-border payments on stablecoins end to end, with the Solana Foundation as technical partner. - @DecryptMedia. Announced The Information Exchange on Solana: news, prediction markets and trading on the same page. Fully live before Breakpoint. - @Raydium. A record $2.8B in tokenized-stock trading in September, then past $6B all-time. - New listings. BlackRock, Nokia, Rocket Lab and Bloom Energy via @Backpack, Quant via @Sunrise, and Coinbase's cbADA. Nokia traded $11.45M in its first 45 minutes. - Network activity. About 3.2B successful non-vote transactions in September, a third straight monthly record, and a record 8.92B for the quarter. - Lending. More tokenized stocks are posted as collateral on Solana than any other chain: $20.7M of xStocks on @Kamino, more than three times Ethereum. Follow @tokens for tokenization and Solana ecosystem news.

Here’s everything that happened this week: 📰 **Headline News** \- [@Fiserv](https://x.com/Fiserv)’s digital asset platform launched on Solana, enabling Roughrider Coin transfers across 90+ banks and records.author: Present_Let2487
records.title: Has a transaction preview ever stopped you from signing something bad? (r/solana)
records.content: - I’ll admit I approve transactions without really reading the preview. Last week the preview flagged that a transaction was moving a token I hadn't mentioned anywhere in the trade. When I took a closer look, it was just some account being closed and rent coming back. But yeah, for about ten seconds I was convinced I’d signed something sketchy. Since then I've been reading transaction previews properly, and I've noticed how much they vary between wallets. Some spell out exactly what's leaving while some show a wall of program calls that mean nothing to me. Has a transaction preview ever stopped you from signing something malicious? Also, if you read every transaction before approving it, did the technical stuff make sense, or do you mostly learn what looks suspicious?
